'''Shohini Ghose''' is a quantum physicist and Professor of Physics and Computer Science at [[Wilfrid Laurier University]].<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date= |title=Dr. Shohini Ghose |url=https://www.wlu.ca/academics/faculties/faculty-of-science/faculty-profiles/shohini-ghose/index.html?ref=science%2Fsghose |access-date=2019-11-17 |website=www.wlu.ca}}</ref> She has served as the president of the [[Canadian Association of Physicists]] (2019-2020),<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |title=Home |url=https://www.cap.ca/ |access-date=2019-11-17 |website=Canadian Association of Physicists |language=en-US}}</ref> co-editor-in-chief of the [[Canadian Journal of Physics]],<ref name=":22">{{Cite web |title=Canadian Journal of Physics |url=https://www.nrcresearchpress.com/loi/cjp |access-date=2019-11-17 |website=www.nrcresearchpress.com}}</ref> and the Director of the Laurier Centre for Women in Science.<ref name=":02" /> She was named a 2014 [[TED (conference)|TED Fellow]]<ref name=":32">{{Cite web |title=TED Fellows Program |url=https://www.ted.com/participate/ted-fellows-program |access-date=2019-11-17 |website=www.ted.com |language=en}}</ref> and a 2018 [[TED Fellow|TED Senior Fellow]].<ref name=":42">{{Cite web |title=Laurier Professor Shohini Ghose named TED Senior Fellow {{!}} Wilfrid Laurier University |url=https://www.wlu.ca/news/news-releases/2018/jan/laurier-professor-shohini-ghose-named-ted-senior-fellow.html |access-date=2019-11-17 |website=www.wlu.ca}}</ref> In 2019 she appeared on the Star TV show TED Talks India Nayi Baat hosted by [[Shah Rukh Khan]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=TED Talks India Nayi Baat |url=https://www.hotstar.com/ca/tv/ted-talks-india/s-1346 |access-date=2019-11-17 |website=Hotstar |language=en}}</ref> In 2017 she was elected to the [[Royal Society of Canada|Royal Society of Canada's College of New Scholars, Artists and Scientists]].<ref name=":52">{{Cite web |title=Laurier professors selected for the College of New Scholars, Artists and Scientists of the Royal Society of Canada {{!}} Wilfrid Laurier University |url=https://www.wlu.ca/news/news-releases/2017/sept/laurier-professors-selected-for-the-college-of-new-scholars-artists-and-scientists-of-the-royal-society-of-canada.html |access-date=2019-11-17 |website=www.wlu.ca}}</ref> Her book [https://www.amazon.in/Clues-Cosmos-Shohini-Ghose/dp/9389305209 Clues to the Cosmos] was released in India in December 2019. In 2020, she was selected as an [[Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council|NSERC]] [[Chair for Women in Science and Engineering]].<ref name="wlu.ca">{{Cite web |title=Laurier quantum physicist selected as NSERC Chair for Women in Science and Engineering {{!}} Wilfrid Laurier University |url=https://www.wlu.ca/news/news-releases/2020/aug/laurier-quantum-physicist-selected-as-nserc-chair-for-women-in-science-and-engineering.html |access-date=2023-10-16 |website=www.wlu.ca}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Ghose grew up in India where she dreamed of becoming an astronaut after finding out about the first Indian astronaut in space.<ref name=":62">{{Cite web |title=Women in Physics: Dr. Shohini Ghose |url=http://blog.cdnsciencepub.com/women-in-physics-dr-shohini-ghose/ |access-date=2019-11-17 |website=Canadian Science Publishing |language=en-US}}</ref> She moved to [[Miami University]] for her undergraduate studies, where she majored in physics and mathematics.<ref name=":62" /> She received her PhD in physics from the [[University of New Mexico]] in 2003.<ref name=":62" /> She was awarded the Chairman's award for best dissertation titled "Quantum And Classical Dynamics Of Atoms In A Magneto‐optical Lattice",<ref>{{Cite web |title=Meet Laurier's Quantum Woman: Shohini Ghose |url=https://www.universityaffairs.ca/news/news-article/look-stage-quantum-woman/ |access-date=2019-11-17 |website=University Affairs |language=en-US}}</ref> which delved into the quantum chaotic behavior of atoms interacting with lasers and magnetic fields.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ghose |first=Shohini |year=2003 |title=Quantum and classical dynamics of atoms in a magneto-optical lattice |journal=Ph.D. Thesis |language=en |volume=676 |pages=283–294 |arxiv=quant-ph/0210131 |bibcode=2003PhDT........63G |doi=10.1063/1.1612224 |s2cid=14461407}}</ref>

== Research and professional activities ==
In 2003, Ghose moved to the [[University of Calgary]] where she held an Alberta Ingenuity Postdoctoral Fellowship.<ref name=":7">{{Cite journal|last1=Lee|first1=Brian L.|last2=Sykes|first2=Brian D.|last3=Fliegel|first3=Larry|title=Structural and functional insights into the cardiac Na+/H+ exchanger|journal=Journal of Molecular and Cellular Cardiology|volume=61|pages=60–67|doi=10.1016/j.yjmcc.2012.11.019|issn=0022-2828|year=2013|pmid=23220151}}</ref> After one year of postdoctoral research, she accepted a position as Assistant Professor at [[Wilfrid Laurier University]] in 2005.<ref name=":62" />  She continued her research in the field of quantum physics, working on [[quantum entanglement]], chaos and tunneling. She is best known for her work with her colleague [[Poul S. Jessen|Poul Jessen]]'s team at the [[University of Arizona]] to make the first ever observations of individual cesium atoms that showed the effect of chaos on quantum entanglement.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nature08396?|title=Quantum signatures of chaos in a kicked top|year=2009 |doi=10.1038/nature08396 |access-date=|last1=Chaudhury |first1=S. |last2=Smith |first2=A. |last3=Anderson |first3=B. E. |last4=Ghose |first4=S. |last5=Jessen |first5=P. S. |journal=Nature |volume=461 |issue=7265 |pages=768–771 |pmid=19812668 |bibcode=2009Natur.461..768C |s2cid=4328230 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> Her research on [[quantum chaos]] was selected for the 2011 McGraw-Hill Yearbook of Science and Technology – an annual collection of breakthroughs in science and technology.<ref>{{cite book | last1=Ghose | first1=Shohini  | last2=Jessen | first2=Poul S. | chapter=Quantum signatures of chaos  | title=McGraw-Hill Yearbook of Science and Technology 2011 | publisher=McGraw-Hill Education | article-url=https://www.accessscience.com/content/article/aYB110098 |article-url-access=subscription |doi = 10.1036/1097-8542.yb110098 | date=2010-12-17 | isbn=978-0-07-176371-4}}</ref>

In 2012 Ghose co-authored the first introductory astronomy textbook in Canada for university students.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news-centre.uwinnipeg.ca/all-posts/uwinnipeg-prof-co-authors-canadas-first-intro-astronomy-textbook/|title=UWinnipeg Prof Co-Authors Canada's First Intro Astronomy Textbook {{!}} University of Winnipeg {{!}} News Centre|date=29 March 2012 |language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> Today her research is focused on [[quantum information science]]. She has published on the topics of quantum communication, teleportation, multiparty quantum correlations and quantum chaos.<ref name=":02"/> She is a Fellow of the [[Balsillie School of International Affairs]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.balsillieschool.ca/shohini-ghose/|title=Shohini Ghose|last=bsia|date=2017-09-09|website=Balsillie School of International Affairs|language=en-CA|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> and is the Co-Editor in Chief (2018-) of the Canadian Journal of Physics.<ref name=":22"/>

In 2019, Ghose's  TED talk “A beginners guide to quantum computing” was featured on TED.com.<ref>{{Citation|last=Ghose|first=Shohini|title=A beginner's guide to quantum computing|date=11 January 2019 |url=https://www.ted.com/talks/shohini_ghose_a_beginner_s_guide_to_quantum_computing|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> In 2014 she gave a [[TED (conference)|TEDx]] talk at [[Greater Sudbury|Nickel City]] titled "Breaking barriers with quantum physics", in 2015 "How Quantum Physics Can Help Us Fight Climate Change" in TEDxVictoria, and in 2016 "The Surprising Power of Uncertainty" at [[Thunder Bay]].<ref>{{Citation|title=Breaking barriers with quantum physics {{!}} Dr. Shohini Ghose {{!}} TEDxNickelCity| date=26 November 2014 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TlmwLyeWv5M|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=How Quantum Physics Can Help Us Fight Climate Change {{!}} Shohini Ghose {{!}} TEDxVictoria| date=11 December 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x02ZKWkexeo|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=The surprising power of uncertainty {{!}} Shohini Ghose {{!}} TEDxThunderBay| date=18 July 2016 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6hizqph2qKQ|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> She spoke at the 2015 [[Smithsonian Institution]] Future is Here Festival on "Alice in Quantum Wonderland".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.smithsonianmag.com/videos/category/future-is-here/future-is-here-festival-2015-shohini-ghose/|title=Alice in Quantum Wonderland|website=www.smithsonianmag.com|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> She has been featured in several online science videos including on BBC and PBS Nova.<ref name=":02"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b0bb33ht|title=BBC Two - Horizon, 2018, How to Build a Time Machine|website=BBC|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref><ref name="bbc.co.uk">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/w3csytgh|title=BBC World Service - The Inquiry, Why the race to build a quantum computer?|website=BBC|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref>

Ghose was one of few women in her PhD physics program. Her experiences led her in 2012 to found Laurier's University Research Centre for Women in Science (WinS), whose mission is to build a strong community for women in science through research, communication, and action.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://researchcentres.wlu.ca/centre-for-women-in-science/index.html|title=Laurier Centre for Women in Science {{!}} Wilfrid Laurier University|website=researchcentres.wlu.ca|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> The Centre supports research in science and social science, provides resources and mentorship to other organizations, organizes and sponsors conferences, workshops and outreach activities, facilitates networking, and helps develop policy and actions to address structural and social barriers in science. In the WinS research exhibit #DistractinglyHonest, [[Wilfrid Laurier University]] researcher Eden Hennessey explored sexism in science.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wlu.ca/news/news-releases/2016/sept/lauriers-distractinglyhonest-photo-research-exhibit-addresses-sexism-in-science.html|title=Laurier's #DistractinglyHonest photo-research exhibit addresses sexism in science {{!}} Wilfrid Laurier University|website=www.wlu.ca|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> The WinS platform #MySTEMStory explores women's lives in physics. In 2015 Ghose gave a TEDx talk titled, "What if Einstein had been a woman?".<ref>{{Citation|title=What if Einstein had been a woman? {{!}} Shohini Ghose {{!}} TEDxWaterlooWomen| date=21 May 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7IZmDPm8yJ8|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> In 2016 she delivered an INKTalk "Women scientists you've never heard of",<ref>{{Citation|title=Shohini Ghose: Women scientists you've never heard of| date=5 August 2015 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4qpeEJCUeZ8|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> and created a [[TEDed|TED-Ed]] video on [[Marie Curie]].<ref>{{Citation|title=The genius of Marie Curie - Shohini Ghose| date=8 June 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w6JFRi0Qm_s|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref>

Ghose serves on various advisory councils and panels, and has served as a consultant to academia, industry and government on the importance of equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) in science.<ref name=":02"/> She is an affiliate of the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]] and served as the Institute's first Equity Diversity and Inclusion Specialist from 2018-2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/news/perimeter-ramps-efforts-support-greater-diversity|title=Perimeter ramps up efforts to support greater diversity {{!}} Perimeter Institute|website=www.perimeterinstitute.ca|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> She was part of the advisory team that developed the Dimensions Charter - the Canadian national charter on EDI, and spoke at the launch of the charter in 2019 with Canada's Minister of Science.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/5-3m-in-federal-funding-to-help-universities-improve-equity-diversity-and-inclusion-1.5130884|title=$5.3M in federal funding to help universities improve equity, diversity and inclusion|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref> She is the first Canadian member of the Working Group on Women in Physics of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://iupap.org/working-groups/wg5-women-in-physics/|title=WG5: Women in Physics {{!}} IUPAP: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics|website=iupap.org|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> This group has organized the largest global surveys of the status of women in physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aip.org/statistics/reports/global-survey-physicists|title=Global Survey of Physicists|date=2012-02-19|website=www.aip.org|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref> Ghose is the first person of color to be elected President of the [[Canadian Association of Physicists]] (CAP).<ref name=":12"/> In this role she has created and chaired a standing committee to embed EDI in all activities of the CAP across Canada.<ref name=":12"/>

In 2020, Ghose was chosen to be one of the five [[Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council]] (NSERC) regional Chairs for Women in Science and Engineering.<ref name="wlu.ca"/> A [[Wilfrid Laurier University]] press release stated that "In collaboration with her fellow chairs in Atlantic Canada, Quebec, the Prairies, British Columbia and Yukon, Ghose will lead a national and regional effort to increase the participation and retention of women in science and engineering."<ref name="wlu.ca"/>

In 2023, she published Her Space, Her Time: How Trailblazing Women Scientists Decoded the Hidden Universe<ref>{{Cite book |last=Ghose |first=Shohini |title=Her space, her time: how trailblazing women scientists decoded the hidden universe |date=2023 |publisher=The MIT press |isbn=978-0-262-04831-6 |location=Cambridge}}</ref> with [[MIT Press]], which won a SWCC 2023 Book Award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 Book Awards |url=https://sciencewriters.ca/bookawards2023 |access-date=2025-11-01 |website=sciencewriters.ca}}</ref>

Ghose has won the [[Wilfrid Laurier University]] Merit Award several times (2010, 2015, 2016, 2018) for outstanding research/teaching/service.

2004 - Alberta Ingenuity Fellowship<ref name=":7" />

2011 - Shera Bangali Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/entertainment/shera-bangali-2011/cid/368190|title=Shera Bangali 2011|website=www.telegraphindia.com|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref>

2014 - Gifted Citizen<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL4FvZzvOvAPin80kjF5b-GqFOnfiFyQ8_|title=GIFTED CITIZEN COMMUNITY - YouTube|website=YouTube|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref>

2014 - Mahatma Gandhi Global Achievers award<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thecord.ca/ghost-seen-as-a-global-achiever/|title=Ghose seen as a 'global' achiever|last=|first=|date=5 November 2014|website=thecord.ca|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://issuu.com/wilfridlaurieruniversity/docs/campus_winter_2014_web/41|title=Winter 2014 Campus Magazine|website=Issuu|date=28 November 2014 |language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref>

2014 - Women of Waterloo (WOW) Education Award<ref>{{Citation|title=Dr Shohini Ghose - Education| date=3 May 2014 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eQYUQBMIzZM|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref>

2014 - [[American Physical Society]] Women Physicist of the Month<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://services.cap.ca/drupal/sites/cap.ca/files/article/2917/pic-70-1-congratulations.pdf|title=SHOHINI GHOSE NAMED PHYSICIST OF THE MONTH FOR APRIL 2014|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/women/reports/gazette/upload/spring15.pdf|title=Committee on the Status of Women in Physics Newsletter|last=|first=|date=|website=|access-date=}}</ref>

2014 - [[TED Fellow]]<ref name=":32"/>

2015 - Indo-Canadians ''The A List''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://newsroom.carleton.ca/archives/2015/02/06/carleton-celebrates-new-list-indo-canadians-friends-india/|title=Carleton Celebrates New A-List of Indo-Canadians and Friends of India|date=2015-02-06|website=Carleton Newsroom Archives|language=en-US|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref>

2016 - Rogers Woman of the Year Award<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://womenoftheyear.oktoberfest.ca/award-recipients/|title=K-W Oktoberfest Rogers Women of the Year: 2016 Award Recipients|website=womenoftheyear.oktoberfest.ca|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.therecord.com/news-story/6901572-oktoberfest-women-of-the-year/|title=Oktoberfest Women of the Year|last=staff|first=Record|date=2016-10-07|website=TheRecord.com|language=en-CA|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref>

2017 - Inductee, Royal Society of Canada, College of New Scholars, Artists and Scientists<ref name=":52"/>

2018 - Faculty of Science Award for Teaching Excellence, Wilfrid Laurier University<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wlu.ca/academics/faculties/faculty-of-science/news/2018/fall/faculty-of-science-recognizes-shohini-ghose-for-excellence-in-teaching.html|title=Faculty of Science recognizes Shohini Ghose for excellence in teaching {{!}} Wilfrid Laurier University|website=www.wlu.ca|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref>

2018 - Senior [[TED Fellow]]<ref name=":42"/>

2019 - Featured among 25 women from around the world in UNESCO exhibit, Paris, France: ‘Remarkable Women in Technology<ref>{{Citation|last=Equality|first=UNESCO's Priority Gender|title=19 Shohini Ghose|date=2019-03-06|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/153162102@N06/32355786937/|access-date=2019-11-17}}</ref>
